## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Awadhi native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Awadhi a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Balinese Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Balinese
- **ISO 639 code**: ban
- **Script**: Balinese
- **Native speakers**: 3.3M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Balinese-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Balinese keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Balinese native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Balinese a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Balochi Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Balochi
- **ISO 639 code**: bal
- **Script**: Perso-Arabic
- **Native speakers**: 8M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Balochi-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Balochi keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Balochi native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Balochi a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Batak Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Batak
- **ISO 639 code**: btk
- **Script**: Batak
- **Native speakers**: 2M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Batak-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Batak keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

# Bengali Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Bengali
- **ISO 639 code**: ben
- **Script**: Bengali
- **Native speakers**: 270 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Bengali-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Bengali keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Bengali native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Bengali a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
যদি (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
অন্যথা              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Bhojpuri Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Bhojpuri
- **ISO 639 code**: bho
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 52M

- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Bhojpuri-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Bhojpuri keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Bhojpuri native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Bhojpuri a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Bodo Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Bodo
- **ISO 639 code**: brx
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 1.5M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Bodo-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Bodo keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Bodo native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Bodo a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Buginese Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Buginese
- **ISO 639 code**: bug
- **Script**: Lontara
- **Native speakers**: 5M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Buginese-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Buginese keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Buginese native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Buginese a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Burmese Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Burmese
- **ISO 639 code**: mya
- **Script**: Myanmar
- **Native speakers**: 33M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Burmese-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Burmese keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Burmese native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Burmese a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Chhattisgarhi Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Chhattisgarhi
- **ISO 639 code**: hne
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 18M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Chhattisgarhi-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Chhattisgarhi keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Chhattisgarhi native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Chhattisgarhi a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Dari Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Dari
- **ISO 639 code**: prs
- **Script**: Perso-Arabic
- **Native speakers**: 12M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Dari-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Dari keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Dari native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Dari a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Dogri Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Dogri
- **ISO 639 code**: doi
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 2.6M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Dogri-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Dogri keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

| `KW_INVARIANT` | invariant | अपरिवर्त्य | `aparivartya` | contract |
| `KW_ASSERT` | assert | प्रतिज्ञा | `pratijnyaa` | contract |
| `KW_ASSUME` | assume | अध्यवस्यति | `adhyavasyati` | contract |
| `KW_PROVE` | prove | साधयति | `saadhayati` | contract |
| `KW_REFINES` | refines | परिष्करोति | `pari_skarauti` | contract |
| `KW_MODEL_CHECK` | modelcheck | प्रतिमानपरीक्षा | `pratimaanapariik_saa` | contract |

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Dogri native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Dogri a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Dzongkha Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Dzongkha
- **ISO 639 code**: dzo
- **Script**: Tibetan
- **Native speakers**: 650K
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Dzongkha-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Dzongkha keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Gujarati native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Gujarati a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
જો (x > 0)        // romenagri: jau
    ...
નહીંતર              // romenagri: nahii_ntara
    ...
```

# Hausa (Ajami) Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Hausa (Ajami)
- **ISO 639 code**: hau
- **Script**: Ajami
- **Native speakers**: 80M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Hausa (Ajami)-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Hausa (Ajami) keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Hausa (Ajami) native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Hausa (Ajami) a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Hebrew Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Hebrew
- **ISO 639 code**: heb
- **Script**: Hebrew
- **Native speakers**: 9 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Hebrew-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Hebrew keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Hebrew native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Hebrew a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
אם (x > 0)        // romenagri: ama
    ...
אחרת              // romenagri: aharata
    ...
```

# Hindi Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Hindi
- **ISO 639 code**: hin
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 600 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Hindi-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Hindi keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Hindi native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Hindi a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Javanese Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Javanese
- **ISO 639 code**: jav
- **Script**: Javanese
- **Native speakers**: 82M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Javanese-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Javanese keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Javanese native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Javanese a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Kannada Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Kannada
- **ISO 639 code**: kan
- **Script**: Kannada
- **Native speakers**: 60 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Kannada-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Kannada keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Kannada native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Kannada a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
ಆದರೆ (x > 0)        // romenagri: aadaree
    ...
ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ              // romenagri: illadiddaree
    ...
```

# Kashmiri (Devanagari) Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Kashmiri (Devanagari)
- **ISO 639 code**: kas
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 7M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Kashmiri (Devanagari)-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Kashmiri (Devanagari) keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Kashmiri (Devanagari) native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Kashmiri (Devanagari) a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Kashmiri Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Kashmiri
- **ISO 639 code**: kas
- **Script**: Perso-Arabic
- **Native speakers**: 7M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Kashmiri-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Kashmiri keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Kashmiri native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Kashmiri a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Khmer Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Khmer
- **ISO 639 code**: khm
- **Script**: Khmer
- **Native speakers**: 16M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Khmer-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Khmer keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Konkani native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Konkani a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Kurdish (Sorani) Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Kurdish (Sorani)
- **ISO 639 code**: ckb
- **Script**: Perso-Arabic
- **Native speakers**: 8M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Kurdish (Sorani)-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Kurdish (Sorani) keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Kurdish (Sorani) native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Kurdish (Sorani) a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Lao Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Lao
- **ISO 639 code**: lao
- **Script**: Lao
- **Native speakers**: 30M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Lao-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Lao keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Lao native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Lao a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Lepcha Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Lepcha
- **ISO 639 code**: lep
- **Script**: Lepcha
- **Native speakers**: 66K
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Lepcha-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Lepcha keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Lepcha native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Lepcha a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Limbu Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Limbu
- **ISO 639 code**: lif
- **Script**: Limbu
- **Native speakers**: 340K
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Limbu-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Limbu keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Limbu native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Limbu a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Magahi Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Magahi
- **ISO 639 code**: mag
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 21M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Magahi-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Magahi keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Magahi native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Magahi a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Maithili Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Maithili
- **ISO 639 code**: mai
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 34M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Maithili-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Maithili keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Maithili native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Maithili a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Malayalam Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Malayalam
- **ISO 639 code**: mal
- **Script**: Malayalam
- **Native speakers**: 38 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Malayalam-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Malayalam keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Malayalam native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Malayalam a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
എങ്കിൽ (x > 0)        // romenagri: e_nkila
    ...
അല്ലെങ്കിൽ              // romenagri: alle_nkila
    ...
```

# Malay (Jawi) Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Malay (Jawi)
- **ISO 639 code**: msa
- **Script**: Jawi
- **Native speakers**: 20M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Malay (Jawi)-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Malay (Jawi) keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

|---|---|---|---|---|

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Malay (Jawi) native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Malay (Jawi) a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Mandaic Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Mandaic
- **ISO 639 code**: mid
- **Script**: Mandaic
- **Native speakers**: liturgical
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Mandaic-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Mandaic keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Mandaic native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Mandaic a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Manipuri (Bengali) Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Manipuri (Bengali)
- **ISO 639 code**: mni
- **Script**: Bengali
- **Native speakers**: 1.8M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Manipuri (Bengali)-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Manipuri (Bengali) keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Manipuri (Bengali) native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Manipuri (Bengali) a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
যদি (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
অন্যথা              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Marathi Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Marathi
- **ISO 639 code**: mar
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 83 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Marathi-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Marathi keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Marathi native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Marathi a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
जर (x > 0)        // romenagri: jara
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Marwari Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Marwari
- **ISO 639 code**: mwr
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 30M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Marwari-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Marwari keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Marwari native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Marwari a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Nabataean Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Nabataean
- **ISO 639 code**: arc
- **Script**: Nabataean
- **Native speakers**: historical
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Nabataean-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Nabataean keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Nabataean native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Nabataean a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Nepali Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Nepali
- **ISO 639 code**: nep
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 32 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Nepali-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Nepali keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Nepali native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Nepali a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Newari Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Newari
- **ISO 639 code**: new
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 860K
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Newari-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Newari keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

| `KW_PROVE` | prove | साधयति | `saadhayati` | contract |
| `KW_REFINES` | refines | परिष्करोति | `pari_skarauti` | contract |
| `KW_MODEL_CHECK` | modelcheck | प्रतिमानपरीक्षा | `pratimaanapariik_saa` | contract |

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Newari native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Newari a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Odia Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Odia
- **ISO 639 code**: ori
- **Script**: Odia
- **Native speakers**: 38 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Odia-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Odia keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Odia native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Odia a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
ଯଦି (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
ଅନ୍ୟଥା              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Pali Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Pali
- **ISO 639 code**: pli
- **Script**: Devanagari (also Sinhala, Thai, Burmese, Khmer historically)
- **Native speakers**: liturgical (Theravada Buddhist canon)
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Pali-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Pali keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

| `KW_ASSUME` | assume | अध्यवस्यति | `adhyavasyati` | contract |
| `KW_PROVE` | prove | साधयति | `saadhayati` | contract |
| `KW_REFINES` | refines | परिष्करोति | `pari_skarauti` | contract |
| `KW_MODEL_CHECK` | modelcheck | प्रतिमानपरीक्षा | `pratimaanapariik_saa` | contract |

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Pali native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Pali a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
सचे (x > 0)        // romenagri: sacee
    ...
अञ्ञथा              // romenagri: anyanyathaa
    ...
```

# Pashto Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Pashto
- **ISO 639 code**: pus
- **Script**: Perso-Arabic
- **Native speakers**: 60M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Pashto-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Pashto keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Persian native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Persian a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
اگر (x > 0)        // romenagri: agar
    ...
وگرنه              // romenagri: vagarnah
    ...
```

# Phoenician Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Phoenician
- **ISO 639 code**: phn
- **Script**: Phoenician
- **Native speakers**: historical (parent of the alphabet)
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Phoenician-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Phoenician keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Phoenician native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Phoenician a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
𐤀𐤌 (x > 0)        // romenagri: ama
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Prakrit Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Prakrit
- **ISO 639 code**: pra
- **Script**: Devanagari (historically Brahmi)
- **Native speakers**: classical/literary (Jain canon, drama)
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Prakrit-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Prakrit keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Prakrit native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Prakrit a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
जइ (x > 0)        // romenagri: jai
    ...
अण्णहा              // romenagri: a_n_nahaa
    ...
```

# Punjabi Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Punjabi
- **ISO 639 code**: pan
- **Script**: Gurmukhi
- **Native speakers**: 125 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Punjabi-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Punjabi keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Punjabi native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Punjabi a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
ਜੇ (x > 0)        // romenagri: jee
    ...
ਨਹੀਂਤਾਂ              // romenagri: nahii_ntaa_n
    ...
```

# Punjabi (Shahmukhi) Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Punjabi (Shahmukhi)
- **ISO 639 code**: pnb
- **Script**: Perso-Arabic
- **Native speakers**: 80M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Punjabi (Shahmukhi)-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Punjabi (Shahmukhi) keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Punjabi (Shahmukhi) native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Punjabi (Shahmukhi) a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Rajasthani Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Rajasthani
- **ISO 639 code**: raj
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 50M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Rajasthani-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Rajasthani keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Rajasthani native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Rajasthani a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Samaritan Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Samaritan
- **ISO 639 code**: smp
- **Script**: Samaritan
- **Native speakers**: liturgical
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Samaritan-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Samaritan keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Samaritan native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Samaritan a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Sanskrit Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Sanskrit
- **ISO 639 code**: san
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: liturgical + scholarly (classical)

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Sanskrit-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Sanskrit keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Sanskrit native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Sanskrit a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Santali-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Santali keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Santali native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Santali a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Saraiki native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Saraiki a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Shan Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Shan
- **ISO 639 code**: shn
- **Script**: Myanmar
- **Native speakers**: 3.3M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Shan-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Shan keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Shan native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Shan a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Sindhi (Devanagari) Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Sindhi (Devanagari)
- **ISO 639 code**: snd
- **Script**: Devanagari
- **Native speakers**: 30M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Sindhi (Devanagari)-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Sindhi (Devanagari) keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Sindhi (Devanagari) native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Sindhi (Devanagari) a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
यदि (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
अन्यथा              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Sindhi Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Sindhi
- **ISO 639 code**: snd
- **Script**: Perso-Arabic
- **Native speakers**: 30M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Sindhi-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Sindhi keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Sindhi native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Sindhi a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
إذا (x > 0)        // romenagri: izaa
    ...
وإلا              // romenagri: vaillaa
    ...
```

# Sinhala Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Sinhala
- **ISO 639 code**: sin
- **Script**: Sinhala
- **Native speakers**: 17M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Sinhala-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Sinhala keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

# Sundanese Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Sundanese
- **ISO 639 code**: sun
- **Script**: Sundanese
- **Native speakers**: 32M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Sundanese-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Sundanese keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Sundanese native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Sundanese a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Syriac native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Syriac a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
ܐܢ (x > 0)        // romenagri: ana
    ...
ܐܚܪܢܐ              // romenagri: aharanaa
    ...
```

# Tagalog Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Tagalog
- **ISO 639 code**: tgl
- **Script**: Baybayin
- **Native speakers**: 28M
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Tagalog-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Tagalog keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Tagalog native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Tagalog a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
yadi (x > 0)        // romenagri: yadi
    ...
anyathaa              // romenagri: anyathaa
    ...
```

# Tamil Programming Language Standard

**ILM / Hindawi Programming System — Per-Language Programming Standard**

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

- **Human language**: Tamil
- **ISO 639 code**: tam
- **Script**: Tamil
- **Native speakers**: 80 million
- **Constructs covered**: 201 of 201
- **Generated**: 2026-05-31

## What this standard defines

This document defines the Tamil-language keyword set for programming across all major paradigms, together with the **Romenagri** ASCII-7 identifier form for each keyword. The Romenagri form is reversible, case-independent, diacritic-free, and legal as a C identifier — which means a compiler or lexer can accept the Tamil keyword directly, in native script, and map it deterministically to the ASCII-7 form for the toolchain.

This is the per-language realisation of the Hindawi Programming System principle: complete systems-programming capability in any human language, with the compiler back-end unchanged.

## Reversibility guarantee

Every Romenagri form in this standard is ASCII-7, contains no uppercase, no diacritics, and matches the C identifier grammar `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`. Each maps back deterministically to its Tamil native-script keyword via the ILM reverse projection (rmn2acii). This is what makes Tamil a first-class systems-programming language, not a localized skin.

## Example

```
எனில் (x > 0)        // romenagri: enila
    ...
இல்லையெனில்              // romenagri: illaiyenila
    ...
```
